title: Fragmented pool lease negotiation and soft-buffer rollout controller
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: During LTS-driven upgrades we observe capacity cliffs in clusters composed of many small heterogeneous GPU islands (fragmented pools). The current 'drain everything then backfill' approach can cause transient request throttling and SLA blips for Dedicated customers. This ticket designs and implements a controller that negotiates temporary lease adjustments with the autoscaler and issues transient soft-buffer credits per pool slice to preserve effective capacity while rolling upgrades across small islands. The controller should: 1) coordinate eviction windows in a sequential, capacity-preserving order; 2) negotiate temporary lease/time-window extensions with autoscaler to prevent bulk scaling reactions; 3) maintain a soft-buffer ledger per tenant/pool-slice that can be consumed by graceful handoffs and restored after upgrade; 4) respect LTS channel pinning and rollout gates to avoid accidental cross-channel migrations.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can walk a fragmented pool topology and compute a safe sequential upgrade order that preserves >=95% effective capacity for high-QoS tenants
Controller communicates lease-adjustments to the autoscaler and receives an explicit ACK before starting each drain window
Soft-buffer credits are minted in the control plane and visible in Console for affected tenants (token-level capacity delta shown)
Canary rollout of the controller across 3 dedicated pools shows no >2 minute SLA regression and zero dropped requests in synthetic replay
Automated rollback triggers if autoscaler ACK not received within negotiated window or if page-in failure rate exceeds threshold
implementation_steps: Design phase: API contract between rollout-controller and autoscaler (RPC + idempotency + lease-token model)
Small PoC: implement in staging the lease-negotiation state machine and simulate fragmented topologies
Migrate soft-buffer ledger into control-plane DB with tenant-scoped balances and audit entries
Implement drain worker that respects lease tokens and backpressure signals from autoscaler
Integrate with LTS channel service so controller only operates on pools eligible for the current channel
Add Console UI elements: soft-buffer balance, predicted capacity impact, per-pool upgrade timeline
End-to-end tests: chaos + load replay across mixed GPU types and tenant priorities
Rollout: gated canary -> progressive rollout with telemetry gating -> global rollout
rollout_plan: Phase A: internal beta on non-customer pools (1 week) -> Phase B: selected customer pools with low-risk tenants (2 weeks) -> Phase C: expanded to 30% of fragmented dedicated fleets (2 weeks) -> Phase D: global. Each phase includes a 48h hold with SLA and error budget checks. Rollout is gate-controlled: channel pinning must be satisfied and autoscaler ACKs must be successful for >90% of target pools before proceeding.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease token lifecycle and idempotent RPCs
Integration tests between rollout-controller and autoscaler shim (staging) to validate ACK/NAK paths
Synthetic replay: traffic replay harness reproducing tenant mix and request patterns with real token-level cost traces
Chaos test: force an autoscaler NAK during a drain window and validate automatic rollback and credit reconciliation
Load soak: 24h soak at production QPS while running sequential drains on 10 fragmented pools
monitoring_and_alerts: Dashboard: per-pool upgrade cadence, soft-buffer utilization, outstanding lease tokens
SLOs: 99th percentile latency and error rate tracked during upgrade windows with automated comparison to baseline
Alerts: autoscaler-ack-timeout (>30s) -> P0 alert; soft-buffer depletion (>80%) -> P1; unexpected backfill spike (>20% above baseline) -> P1
Audit log: immutable entries for minted/consumed soft-buffer credits for compliance and debugging
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: autoscaler refuses lease changes causing blockage -> Mitigation: controller can fallback to conservative draining (slower, smaller windows) and abort on >2 failed attempts
Risk: soft-buffer accounting drift -> Mitigation: nightly reconciliation job and immediate reconciliation on cluster state change
Risk: LTS channel mismatch causes unintended model variant mix -> Mitigation: require explicit channel-compatibility check before issuing lease tokens
Risk: increased control-plane write volume -> Mitigation: batch ledger updates and use optimistic concurrency with backoff
